findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so all database contents, automated snapshots and backups are stored unencrypted at rest.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public IP and makes it reachable from outside the VPC; combined with the admin username and non-encrypted storage this materially expands the attack surface.

The EC2 user_data script writes the database password (var.password) in cleartext into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc, which is served from the web root; user data is also readable via instance metadata. Credentials embedded this way are exposed to anyone with instance or metadata access.

The policy attached to the catalog app role grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", i.e. full administrative control over storage, compute and database services. If the instance is compromised, the attacker can pivot to the entire account.
The master username is the well-known default "admin", which reduces the effort required for credential guessing/brute force against a publicly accessible database.

The database security group egress rule allows all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting the DB instance to initiate arbitrary outbound connections and facilitating data exfiltration or command-and-control if the instance is compromised.

backup_retention_period = 0 and monitoring_interval = 0 disable automated backups and enhanced monitoring; while primarily operational, the absence of automated backups weakens recovery from tampering or destructive attacks.
